artists.biography: The freshest act to come out of Hull – well, ever – Ryan Smith aka BDRMM has spent the year since debut Crike expanding his outfit from hazy solo project to a full-blown professional band. Between carving out a growing reputation on the Northern circuit via Tramlines and Humber Street Sesh, Smith’s been writing. Six tracks of pure hazy magnificence, Yucky channels all the wavey vibes you could ever desire. Dreamy vocals? Check. Sick as fuck artwork? You bet. The soaring instrumental opener of ‘GCSE Bitesize’ is beautifully reverb-laden, conveying pure tranquility from the get-go. ‘D.a.d’ showcases Smith’s softer side with flawless melodies and idyllic chords; ‘Aw (inter lube)’ is similarly mellow, calling to mind Homeshake with its distorted vocal samples. ‘Paft, dunk’ is the 80’s tune of your dreams with its nostalgic synth and catalytic build – but it’s ‘Happy’ that’s Yucky’s ultimate banger, a Jaws inspired number that catapults you into a whole other universe where ethereal guitars shimmer and effortless vocals build. Melting into the infectious ‘Call (U!) Up’, the EP ends all its magical glory on a resounding high. Yucky is more than a simple collection of feel-good summer tunes; it debuts a unique slice of chillwave aesthetic that sets Smith apart from other industry copycats. With a sound this refined only two EP’s in, there’s only one direction that BDRMM’s going – and that’s up. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Released on February 28, 2025, Microtonic is the third studio album by UK band bdrmm, issued via Rock Action Records. The album marks a notable evolution in the band’s sound, shifting toward a more pronounced electronic focus while retaining their signature blend of shoegaze, post-rock, and ambient textures. Tracks like “Infinity Peaking” and “Clarkycat” showcase a balance between slow, immersive builds and rhythmic, club-inspired instrumentals, reflecting a broader sonic palette that incorporates futuristic and dance-oriented elements. The production is clean and immersive, with frontman Ryan Smith describing the album as the most authentic representation of bdrmm’s current identity.

Microtonic follows bdrmm’s previous releases, including their 2020 debut Bedroom and 2023’s I Don’t Know, both of which established the band’s reputation for atmospheric, introspective rock. With this album, bdrmm further pushes the boundaries of their genre, integrating electronic music influences and crafting a sound that feels both expansive and meticulously detailed. The album received positive critical acclaim upon release, praised for its immersive quality and the band’s ability to evolve while maintaining their core aesthetic. It stands as a significant milestone in bdrmm’s discography, signaling a confident step into new musical territory.
